"""Record the expert-watch investigation; validate unchanged forecast and quotes."""
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib
import json
from openpyxl import load_workbook

ROOT = Path('/workspace')
book = ROOT / 'model/forecast.xlsx'
digest = hashlib.sha256(book.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
prior = json.loads((ROOT / 'analysis/2026-10-12-slip.json').read_text())

def cite(source_id, quote):
    assert quote in (ROOT / 'sources' / (source_id + '.txt')).read_text(), (source_id, quote)
    return dict(source_id=source_id, quote=quote)

expert_limit = cite('email-expert', "The expert's knowledge is dated (left in 2025) and covers one employer.")
expert_mix = cite('email-expert', 'Every 2027 plan I saw assumed accelerator spend grows faster than total capex; buildings were pulled forward in 2025–26.')
expert_third = cite('email-expert', 'Expects custom accelerators at the two largest clouds to reach "roughly a third of new accelerator dollars" by late 2027; would not give a 2026 figure.')
aws_plan = cite('amzn-2026-04-29-release', 'Secured a commitment from OpenAI to consume approximately two gigawatts (GW) of Trainium capacity through AWS infrastructure to power its frontier models and advanced workloads, which begins ramping in 2027.')
aws_mixed = cite('amzn-2026-04-29-release', 'Exceeded $20 billion annual revenue run rate for Amazon’s chips business—inclusive of Graviton, Trainium, and Nitro—which is growing triple-digit percentages year-over-year.')
aws_july = cite('amzn-2026-07-30-release', 'Continued gaining momentum with Trainium, with the two leading AI labs in the world, Anthropic and OpenAI, making multi-year, multi-gigawatt commitments;')
aws_nvda = cite('amzn-2026-04-29-release', 'Landed 2.1 million+ AI chips over the past 12 months, more than half of which were Trainium, and announced one million+ NVIDIA GPUs to be deployed starting in 2026, giving customers the widest range of accelerated compute options.')
tpu = cite('web-fb40041ca0', 'We have signed a limited number of agreements to supply TPU systems to customers who require or provide on-premises infrastructure for specialized, high-scale workloads. In the second quarter of 2026, we began recognizing revenues from these agreements, with the significant majority to be recognized in 2027.')
goog_stock = cite('web-fb40041ca0', 'As of December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026, approximately 60% of technical infrastructure assets were comprised of servers and network equipment.')
goog_projects = cite('web-fb40041ca0', 'our data center construction projects are generally multi-year projects with multiple phases, where we acquire land and buildings, construct buildings, and secure and install servers and network equipment.')
meta_future = cite('web-b8b374a1b1', 'In July 2026, we entered into additional data center leases with lease obligations of approximately $68 billion, which are expected to commence in 2027 and 2028, with lease terms of 18 to 20 years.')
msft_future = cite('web-7e3bfccf0e', 'These leases will commence between fiscal year 2027 and fiscal year 2033 with lease terms of 1 year to 20 years.')
rubin = cite('nvda-2026-08-26-release', 'Announced the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform is ramping into full production with racks running at partners including CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and Nebius.')
channel = cite('channel-oct2026', 'Two respondents said custom accelerators are a rising share of new rack orders at two of the four largest US clouds; neither would quantify it.')

questions = list(prior['open_questions'])
questions[1] = 'How much capex is accelerator systems versus prices, buildings, power and prepayments, and is custom share measured in units, racks or dollars? Late-October mix/cash reconciliations and dated 2027 procurement cohorts would test incremental custom spending and placement of the timing proxy.'
questions[5] = 'Will 2027 accelerator spending grow faster than total capex after separating fresh demand from rollover, and do AWS margins remain resilient? Named equipment/building budgets in late-October commentary and January-February guides, followed by Q1 receipts, would answer.'
questions += [
    'Which employer, plan vintage and current procurement cohort support the expert’s one-third estimate for the two unnamed clouds? Identifiable current plans with custom/total accelerator dollars and late-2027 versus annual scope before January-February guidance would distinguish extrapolation from a grounded share estimate.',
    'How much of disclosed Trainium capacity and external TPU agreements converts into 2027 supplier hardware dollars, at what prices and energization dates? Company shipment/value disclosures in late-October results and 2027 guides would permit comparison with total capex; GW, units, service revenue and asset stocks alone cannot.'
]
note = '''The former planner expects accelerator spending to outgrow total capex and custom silicon to take roughly one-third of new accelerator dollars at two clouds by late 2027. Knowledge ends in 2025 at one employer, and the expert supplies no 2026 figure, employer identity or current budget crosswalk [email-expert].

Current disclosures support identifiable custom-silicon expansion: Amazon’s April release names approximately 2GW of OpenAI Trainium capacity beginning to ramp in 2027, reaffirmed directionally in July [amzn-2026-04-29-release] [amzn-2026-07-30-release]. Alphabet’s Q2 filing describes external TPU supply agreements with most revenue expected in 2027 [web-fb40041ca0]. These are independent company disclosures, not confirmation of the expert’s unnamed plans or one-third estimate.

Neither gives comparable 2027 accelerator-spending and total-capex budgets. GW and chip counts are not dollars; Amazon’s chips revenue includes CPUs and Nitro, while external TPU sales are not Alphabet’s own capex. Meta’s future leases and Alphabet’s multi-year construction also limit a blanket buildings-pulled-forward inference [web-b8b374a1b1] [web-fb40041ca0].

I retain every 2026 input and NVIDIA Q3/Q4 estimates of $102bn/$127bn. The prior custom-silicon tail adjustment and dated-slip allowance already cover stronger, more current evidence; this historical expectation warrants no additional haircut. Named procurement dollars and recognition schedules would move me.

NVIDIA’s long calendar earnings case is unchanged this session: base remains $371.43bn, $4.57bn below street; AMD remains approximately at $14bn consensus.'''
finding = '''Partly supported on direction, unresolved on relative growth and share. Amazon discloses a named OpenAI Trainium commitment beginning to ramp in 2027; July commentary sustains that direction. Alphabet’s Q2 filing describes identifiable external TPU agreements whose significant majority of revenue is expected in 2027. These independently support custom-silicon activity beyond the expert’s historical recollection, but provide neither comparable 2027 hardware-spending/total-capex budgets nor a one-third custom-dollar denominator. AWS GW, chip counts and mixed chips-service revenue cannot substitute for hardware dollars; Alphabet external TPU sales cannot be treated as its own PP&E purchases. Stock equipment mix is not new accelerator-spending flow. Future Meta/MSFT leases and multi-year Alphabet construction do not show buildings cease absorbing funds. The expert’s unnamed employer, plan vintage, current access and two-cloud extrapolation are unverified; late-2027 incremental share is not calendar-2026 or full-year share. No new dated delivery or recognized-revenue evidence accompanies the power warning. Hold the already-adjusted 2026 drivers and quarters; need named current procurement dollars and deployment/control-transfer dates to move.'''

d = dict(
    decision='no_change',
    headline='Current plans support 2027 custom growth, not the expert’s one-third share; NVIDIA base held at $371.43bn',
    note=note,
    stance='Capex budgets exceed street, but deployment slips weaken NVIDIA’s calendar capture; 2027 custom growth lacks a measured spending share.',
    rationale='Partly agree with direction, not quantified share or relative growth. Current named Trainium/TPU disclosures provide a stronger basis than dated single-employer recollection, but no 2026 bridge or comparable 2027 spending denominator. No further probability shift beyond existing custom and delivery allowances is defensible from this item. Move on current customer budgets, custom/total accelerator dollars or supplier recognition schedules.',
    thesis='Hold calendar-2026 capex $682.5bn versus $667.5bn street; NVIDIA DC base $371.43bn versus $376bn (-$4.57bn, -1.22%), AMD GPU approximately $14bn versus $14bn. Base mix/split/concentration remain 37.3%/65%/44.55% for NVIDIA, AMD split/concentration 2.75%/50%. NVIDIA unreported Q3 DC $102bn and own Q4 $127bn versus required $126.58bn remain on record. Directional 2027 custom growth is supported, but no quantified 2027 share forecast is adopted.',
    claims=[
        dict(statement='The expert’s knowledge ends in 2025 and covers one employer.', entities=['MSFT','GOOGL','META','AMZN'], claim_period='October 9, 2026 call; knowledge through 2025', citation=expert_limit),
        dict(statement='The expert recalls plans for accelerator spend to outgrow total capex; this is historical testimony, not current company guidance.', entities=['MSFT','GOOGL','META','AMZN'], claim_period='Historical plans for 2027', citation=expert_mix),
        dict(statement='The one-third expectation concerns late-2027 new accelerator dollars at two unnamed clouds, with no 2026 figure.', entities=['MSFT','GOOGL','META','AMZN','NVDA','AMD'], claim_period='Late 2027 expectation', citation=expert_third),
        dict(statement='Amazon disclosed a named OpenAI Trainium capacity commitment beginning to ramp in 2027; no hardware-dollar share is provided.', entities=['AMZN'], claim_period='April 29, 2026 disclosure; 2027 ramp', citation=aws_plan),
        dict(statement='Alphabet disclosed external TPU agreements, with most associated revenue expected in 2027; these are sales rather than its own capex purchases.', entities=['GOOGL'], claim_period='Q2 2026 disclosure; expected 2027 revenue', citation=tpu),
        dict(statement='Alphabet’s approximately 60% server/network equipment proportion describes an asset stock, not incremental accelerator spending.', entities=['GOOGL'], claim_period='December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026', citation=goog_stock),
    ], capex_changes=[], changes=[],
    implications=[
        dict(company='NVDA', customer='AMZN', relationship_id='aws-nvda', interpretation='Amazon’s April 29, 2026 disclosure places Trainium expansion alongside planned NVIDIA deployment, supporting coexistence and a customer capture risk rather than measured displacement.', uncertainty='Chip units and GW do not establish dollar shares, contract value or recognized NVIDIA revenue; Amazon is not identified as the expert’s former employer or an affected delayed cloud.', evidence=[aws_nvda, aws_plan]),
        dict(company='NVDA', customer='GOOGL', relationship_id='gcp-nvda', interpretation='Alphabet’s dated Q2 TPU agreements and NVIDIA’s August 26 Google Cloud Rubin relationship anchor competing accelerator offerings.', uncertainty='External TPU sales may serve customers outside the modeled four. They do not establish Google’s own custom procurement share, displacement of NVIDIA, or the expert’s unnamed-cloud identity.', evidence=[tpu, rubin]),
    ],
    uncertainties=[
        'The expert’s employer, plan dates, revisions and access after departure are unspecified; one-employer knowledge cannot establish two clouds’ current budgets.',
        'Late-2027 marginal share is not full-year share, and neither is calendar-2026 share.',
        'No comparable 2027 accelerator-spending and total-capex budgets were found in reviewed disclosures.',
        'GW, chip units, mixed service revenue, external TPU sales and equipment asset stocks have different denominators from procurement dollars.',
        'A different vendor/source family does not prove independent underlying plans or respondent knowledge.',
        'Existing anonymous delivery, cash-capex and supplier-control-transfer uncertainties remain open; the expert provides no new dated order confirmation.',
    ],
    catalysts=[
        'Late October 2026: customer capex guides, equipment/building mix, named custom procurement and 2027 commentary.',
        'Early November 2026, expected: AMD recognized GPU revenue and customer shipment timing.',
        'November 18, 2026, expected/unconfirmed: NVIDIA Q3 DC versus $102bn and Q4 guide versus own $127bn/required $126.58bn.',
        'January-February 2027: comparable customer total-capex and accelerator budgets; named Trainium/TPU deployment value and power-ready dates.',
    ],
    disconfirming_evidence=[
        'Named current Trainium and TPU commitments support custom growth despite limitations of the expert account.',
        'Amazon also plans NVIDIA deployments, and Google Cloud appears in NVIDIA’s Rubin disclosure; custom growth does not by itself establish supplier volume decline.',
        'Future data-center leases and multi-year construction limit generalizing that buildings were already pulled forward across all clouds.',
        'Deferred 2026 orders can inflate 2027 growth without additional underlying demand.',
    ],
    evidence=[expert_limit, expert_third, aws_mixed, aws_july, goog_projects, meta_future, msft_future, channel],
    investigation=dict(
        question='Do current company disclosures support accelerator spending outgrowing total capex in 2027, and is the expert’s one-third custom expectation grounded in identifiable plans?',
        reason='Separate current named plans from dated one-employer recollection, and distinguish hardware procurement dollars from capacity, units, service revenues and asset stocks before changing supplier capture.',
        searches=['2027 accelerator spending custom silicon capex plans','Trainium TPU Maia MTIA custom silicon one third','2027 capex servers technical infrastructure accelerator','2027 Trainium TPU Maia MTIA','capital expenditures 2027 buildings servers mix','one third custom accelerator dollars 2027','2027 accelerator total capital expenditures mix (public sources)','Maia MTIA custom accelerator roadmap (public sources)','Attempted official Microsoft FY2026 Q4 earnings-call transcript fetch; HTTP 404'],
        sources_read=['email-expert','amzn-2026-04-29-release','amzn-2026-07-30-release','googl-2026-02-04-release','googl-2026-07-22-release','web-fb40041ca0','meta-2026-07-29-release','web-b8b374a1b1','msft-2026-07-29-release','web-7e3bfccf0e','nvda-2026-08-26-release','amd-2026-08-04-release','channel-oct2026','channel-q4-slip'],
        finding=finding, status='partially_answered'),
    open_questions=questions, follow_up=None, attention=None,
    upcoming_reports=[dict(company='NVDA',date='2026-11-18',source_id=None)],
)
assert 120 <= len(note.split()) <= 250, len(note.split())
assert len(d['stance'].split()) <= 25
(ROOT / 'analysis/2026-10-12-expert.json').write_text(json.dumps(d,ensure_ascii=False,indent=2)+'\n')

w = load_workbook(book, data_only=False)
inputs = {'C4':150,'C5':180,'C6':137.5,'C7':215,
          'B11':.353,'C11':.373,'D11':.39,'B12':.64,'C12':.65,'D12':.655,
          'B13':.025,'C13':.0275,'D13':.03,'B14':.4485,'C14':.4455,'D14':.445,
          'B15':.55,'C15':.5,'D15':.45}
for cell, value in inputs.items():
    assert w['Inputs'][cell].value == value
for cell,value in {'B7':62.314,'C7':75.246,'D7':89.023,'E7':102,'B15':127,
                   'B10':'nvda-2026-02-25-cfo','C10':'nvda-2026-05-20-cfo','D10':'nvda-2026-08-26-cfo','E10':'channel-q4-slip'}.items():
    assert w['Quarters'][cell].value == value
assert w['Quarters']['F7'].data_type == 'f' and w['Quarters']['B12'].value == '=Model!C4'
assert all(w['Model'][f'{col}{row}'].data_type=='f' for col in 'BCD' for row in range(3,10))
assert w['Consensus']['B4'].value == 376 and w['Consensus']['B5'].value == 14

questions_text = '# Open questions — October 12, 2026, expert-watch update\n\n'
questions_text += '\n\n'.join(f'{i}. {q}' for i,q in enumerate(questions,1))
questions_text += '''\n\nAnswered on stated scope: current company disclosures identify Trainium/TPU expansion and expected 2027 activity. They do not establish accelerator-spending growth relative to total capex, the expert's one-third share, or the identities/revenue/cash timing of prior deferrals. All fourteen prior questions are carried forward; two questions specify the expert's grounding and procurement-dollar conversion.

Next independent session: none scheduled immediately; await current company budgets or vendor plan/order crosswalks. Prior analyst attention on the dated-slip crosswalk remains recorded, not re-raised by this historical expert account.
'''
(ROOT/'notes/open-questions.md').write_text(questions_text)

tp = ROOT/'notes/thesis.md'
thesis = tp.read_text()
thesis = thesis.replace('As of 2026-10-12T14:41:18+00:00.', 'As of 2026-10-12T15:02:34+00:00; inputs last revised at 14:41 on the dated delivery-slip check.')
thesis = thesis.replace('**Stance:** Current-year accelerator realization weakens despite larger forward orders; NVIDIA falls further below street, while AMD stays near consensus.', '**Stance:** ' + d['stance'])
thesis = thesis.replace('Fourteen forecast questions remain', 'Sixteen forecast questions remain')
section = '''## Expert check — current plans versus historical expectations

The October 9 expert call comes from a distinct fictional network, but knowledge ends in 2025 at one unidentified employer. Its late-2027 one-third expectation for new accelerator dollars at two unnamed clouds gives no current plan dates, procurement denominator or 2026 figure. Different source families do not establish independent underlying plans. Do not map these anonymous clouds to Amazon/Alphabet [email-expert].

Current primary disclosures partly support direction. Amazon's April 29 release names approximately 2GW of OpenAI Trainium capacity beginning to ramp in 2027; July sustains multi-year Trainium commitments. Alphabet's Q2 filing describes external TPU supply agreements with the significant majority of associated revenue expected in 2027. These establish named activity, not a third of procurement dollars. AWS chips revenue includes Graviton/Trainium/Nitro; chip counts and GW are not dollars. Alphabet's external sales are not its own PP&E purchases, and its 60% server/network asset proportion is stock rather than incremental accelerator flow [amzn-2026-04-29-release] [amzn-2026-07-30-release] [web-fb40041ca0].

No reviewed disclosure provides comparable 2027 accelerator and total-capex budgets. Meta's new leases commencing 2027–28, Microsoft's FY2027–33 leases and Alphabet's multi-year projects limit a universal buildings-pulled-forward inference, but are not replacement annual capex guides. The expert's power observation supplies no new date/order evidence beyond the already-adjusted slip [web-b8b374a1b1] [web-7e3bfccf0e] [web-fb40041ca0] [channel-q4-slip].

Hold every calendar-2026 input and recorded quarter. Current direction agrees with the prior custom-risk tail adjustment; stale unquantified marginal-2027 expectations do not justify another haircut. Move on named current custom/total accelerator dollars, revised guides, recognized supplier shipments or deployment/control-transfer schedules. No 2027 one-third forecast is adopted. Identifiable activity is supported; relative growth and quantified share remain unresolved.

'''
if '## Expert check — current plans versus historical expectations' not in thesis:
    thesis = thesis.replace('## NVIDIA numbers on record', section+'## NVIDIA numbers on record')
    thesis = thesis.replace('- January–March 2027:', '- January–February 2027: comparable accelerator/total-capex budgets and named custom deployment values to test the expert estimate.\n- January–March 2027:')
    thesis += "\nExpert-watch position update: no further change to NVIDIA's 2026 long earnings case; base stays 371.43, gap -4.57 (-1.22%). AMD base stays approximately 14 street. Long-term custom capture remains a risk, not a newly quantified shortfall. No new attention trigger; the prior vendor-crosswalk question remains pending.\n"
tp.write_text(thesis)

run='e0c17efdf8bd4682aee1141b8a15f61b'
post=f"\n## 2026-10-12T15:02:34+00:00 — {d['headline']}\n\nRun: {run}. Item: email-expert, synthetic watch item.\n\n{note}\n\nInvestigation: {d['investigation']['question']} Status: partially answered.\n\nFinding: {finding}\n\n"
post += '''What was checked: searched 2027 capex/accelerator mix, custom roadmaps, one-third shares and named procurement. Read latest July customer releases, Alphabet Q2 filing's TPU revenue and capital-expenditure sections, Meta/MSFT future leases, April-to-July Trainium language, NVIDIA/AMD dated relationships and both channel checks. Attempted official Microsoft FY26 Q4 transcript retrieval returned HTTP 404; do not infer missing guidance from that failure. Eligible releases/SEC filings supplied the reviewed primary evidence. No current customer spending denominator or identified expert plan was found.

Evidence assessment: independent company disclosures ground custom-silicon activity, not the expert's anonymous plans or precise share. AWS planned 2GW starts ramping in 2027, not a disclosed completion date/value; TPU expected sales are outside purchasers' on-premises infrastructure rather than Alphabet own PP&E. Aggregate chips revenue includes CPUs/Nitro and recurring services; hardware counts and asset-stock proportions are not marginal dollars. Meta/MSFT lease obligations and commencement windows are not annual capex or power-ready dates. Late-2027 incremental share is not an annual average or calendar-2026 input. No new confirmation of the prior 12–15bn orders was obtained.

Decision: hold all 19 capex/driver input cells, reported quarters and Q3 estimate102/ownQ4127. NVIDIA bear/base/bull343.79/371.43/391.79 versus376; AMDbase14.0015 versus14. Base mix37.3%, NVDAshare65%, cohort44.55%; AMDsplit2.75%, cohort50%. Existing custom-risk bull adjustment and dated-delivery realization allowance remain. The current item changes no defensible probability beyond those stronger current signals. Named procurement dollars, current guide changes or supplier control-transfer dates would move the forecast.

Verification: analysis/expert_update.py validates all exact quotes, unchanged input/quarter/source cells, consensus, output formulas and identical workbook SHA-256. compute confirms the held base371.43/AMD14.00; requiredQ4126.5847 versus own127 remains plausible under the documented monthly approximation. analysis/2026-10-12-expert-check.json records checks and limitations. No model or quarter mutation was required.

Open: all fourteen previous questions are retained and two specify identifiable expert-plan grounding and custom capacity-to-hardware-dollar conversion. Relative 2027 growth, one-third custom share and current access remain unresolved; direction is partly supported. Sixteen questions and answer dates are in notes/open-questions.md.

Next: no immediate repeat investigation scheduled; await late-October/November disclosures and January-February comparable budgets.

Attention: none. No new crossing, >5% move, guidance conflict or position-specific information need arises from this account. The previous dated-slip vendor-crosswalk request remains recorded without repetition; analyst guidance and decisions are still empty.

Position read: NVIDIA long's 2026 calendar earnings case is unchanged this session; base stays371.43, deficit4.57 (-1.22%) versus376, movement against street0. AMD stays approximately14 street. Custom capture remains a longer-term risk; position decisions belong to the analyst and PM.
'''
lp=ROOT/'notes/research-log.md'
history=lp.read_text()
if run not in history:
    lp.write_text(history+post)
assert digest==hashlib.sha256(book.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
check=dict(as_of='2026-10-12T15:02:34+00:00', decision='no_change', note_words=len(note.split()),
           workbook_sha256=digest, workbook_unchanged=True, all_inputs_verified=True,
           quarters_verified=True, formulas_preserved=True, open_questions=len(questions),
           forecast=dict(NVDA_base_bn=371.4301346801347, AMD_base_bn=14.0014875,
                         q3_dc_bn=102,q4_own_bn=127,q4_required_bn=126.58470202020209),
           independent_plans='Named company activity, not an independent verification of expert share',
           unresolved=['Expert current plan grounding','2027 relative spending growth','One-third dollar denominator'],
           fetch_limit='Microsoft transcript attempt HTTP404; no absence inference')
(ROOT/'analysis/2026-10-12-expert-check.json').write_text(json.dumps(check,indent=2)+'\n')
print(json.dumps(check,indent=2))
